title: Coach Jared Bednar not traveling with Avalanche after taking puck to face vs. Vegas
content:
Colorado Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar won’t travel with his team on its upcoming road trip as he recovers from being hit in the face by a puck during Saturday night’s home game against the Vegas Golden Knights.

Bednar was struck after Golden Knights forward Keegan Kolesar errantly shot the puck into the Avalanche bench. The Avalanche coach suffered facial fractures and a corneal abrasion after the puck hit him on the right side of his face, the team announced in a statement released Sunday morning.

According to the Avalanche, Bednar will not require surgery and is expected to make a full recovery. Assistant coaches Nolan Pratt and Dave Hakstol will coach the Avs in Bednar’s absence.

The Avalanche, who have already clinched the Presidents’ Trophy as the NHL’s best regular-season team this year, will play against the Edmonton Oilers on Monday night before playing the Calgary Flames on Tuesday night. Colorado’s final game of the season is on Thursday night against the Seattle Kraken.
